place.source_title: Downtown Petoskey storefronts with black striped awnings

brief: Two-storey brick storefronts: pale painted brick with tall upper windows, black-and-white striped awnings over a candy shop window, benches and flower tubs. One photo. Older than 1970: Petoskey's Gaslight District (the town's model) is a row of 1880-1910 brick commercial blocks; no newer example of this main-street type exists. Foundations taken deeper than needed (spec rule 4).

facade.notes: downtown Petoskey storefronts (1900): a pink-painted front with a bracketed cornice and the old name panel 'SCATTERGOODS', a café with a black-and-white striped awning, black tile bulkheads, a recessed door, an A-frame sign; brick sidewalk, marigolds

why.note: a revitalised resort-town downtown (Main Street program): street trees, decorative lamps, planters, awnings
